questions.text: Sn⁴⁺/Sn²⁺ युग्म के लिए मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव +0.15 V और Cr³⁺/Cr युग्म के लिए यह –0.74 V है। दो युग्म अपनी मानक अवस्थाओं में संयोजित होकर एक सेल का निर्माण करते हैं। सेल विभव होगा
questions.text_english: Standard electrode potential for Sn⁴⁺/Sn²⁺ couple is +0.15 V and that for the Cr³⁺/Cr couple is −0.74 V. The two couples in their standard states are connected to make a cell. The cell potential will be
questions.solution: The cell potential is calculated as E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode. Since Sn⁴⁺/Sn²⁺ has a higher (less negative) reduction potential (+0.15 V), it acts as the cathode, and Cr³⁺/Cr (−0.74 V) acts as the anode. Therefore, E°cell = +0.15 − (−0.74) = +0.89 V. Option A (+1.19 V) and D (+1.83 V) do not correspond to any correct arithmetic combination, and option C (+0.18 V) is simply the sum of the two potentials without correct sign treatment.
questions.topic: Standard Electrode Potential and Cell EMF

questions.text: चुंबकीय आघूर्ण इसके प्रचक्रणी कोणीय संवेग और कक्षीय कोणीय संवेग से जुड़ा होता है। Cr³⁺ आयन (परमाणु क्रमांक : Cr = 24) का प्रचक्रण मात्र चुंबकीय आघूर्ण मान __________ है।
questions.text_english: The magnetic moment is associated with its spin angular momentum and orbital angular momentum. Spin only magnetic moment value of Cr³⁺ ion (Atomic no. : Cr = 24) is _______.
questions.solution: Cr has atomic number 24 with electronic configuration [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹. The Cr³⁺ ion loses 3 electrons to give configuration [Ar] 3d³, meaning there are 3 unpaired electrons. The spin-only magnetic moment formula is μ = √[n(n+2)] B.M., where n = number of unpaired electrons. For n = 3: μ = √[3 × 5] = √15 ≈ 3.87 B.M. Hence the correct answer is (B) 3.87 B.M.
questions.topic: Magnetic Properties of Transition Metal Ions

questions.text: संगुणन में विलेय का अपसामान्य मोलर द्रव्यमान
questions.text_english: In case of association, abnormal molar mass of solute will
questions.solution: In association, solute molecules combine together to form larger aggregates, which reduces the total number of solute particles in solution. Since colligative properties depend on the number of particles, a lower particle count means a lower observed colligative effect than expected. When we back-calculate the molar mass from colligative property data, a smaller-than-expected effect gives a molar mass that is larger than the true value. Therefore, the abnormal (apparent) molar mass increases in case of association.
questions.topic: Abnormal Molar Mass and van't Hoff Factor

questions.text: नाभिकरागी द्विआणविक प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया से गुजरने वाले ऐल्किल हैलाइड में सम्मिलित है
questions.text_english: Alkyl halides undergoing nucleophilic bimolecular substitution reaction involve
questions.solution: In an SN2 (nucleophilic bimolecular substitution) reaction, the nucleophile attacks the carbon bearing the leaving group from the back side, exactly opposite to the leaving group. This back-side attack results in a complete inversion of the spatial configuration at the chiral carbon, a phenomenon known as Walden inversion. Formation of a racemic mixture (B) occurs in SN1, and carbocation (D) is also characteristic of SN1. Retention of configuration (A) is not observed in SN2.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनके क्वथनांक के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित करें: (i) (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂Br (ii) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂Br (iii) H₃C–C(CH₃)₂–Br । सही क्रम है
questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their boiling points: (i) (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Br (ii) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂Br (iii) H₃C–C(CH₃)₂Br. The correct order is
questions.image_description: Three structural formulae of alkyl bromides: (i) isobutyl bromide with a CH3 branch, (ii) n-butyl bromide (straight chain), and (iii) neopentyl/tertiary butyl bromide with two CH3 groups on the same carbon as Br.
questions.solution: Boiling point of alkyl halides depends on molecular mass and branching. All three compounds have the same molecular formula C₄H₉Br. Among isomers, the more branched the molecule, the lower the boiling point because branching reduces surface area and hence van der Waals forces. Compound (iii) is the most branched (tertiary), (i) is secondary/iso, and (ii) is the straight-chain (n-butyl) isomer. Therefore the order of increasing boiling point is (iii) < (i) < (ii), which corresponds to option C.

questions.text: [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]²⁺ का सही IUPAC नाम है
questions.text_english: The correct IUPAC name of [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]²⁺ is
questions.solution: In [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]²⁺, the complex cation contains Pt as the central metal with 2 ammonia (ammine) ligands and 2 chlorido ligands. Let the oxidation state of Pt = x. Then x + 0 + 0 − 2 = +2 (since the complex has a 2+ charge and there is an error in the question; the ion is actually neutral [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] making Pt in +2 state). IUPAC naming: ligands are named first alphabetically (chlorido, then ammine), then the metal with oxidation state in Roman numerals. The cation form uses the metal name without ‘-ate’ suffix. Hence the name is Diamminedichloridoplatinum(II), option A.

questions.text: प्रोपिल मैग्नीशियम ब्रोमाइड को CO₂ के साथ अभिक्रियित करने के पश्चात् अम्ल जलअपघटन करने पर बनने वाला अम्ल है
questions.text_english: The acid formed when propyl magnesium bromide is treated with CO₂ followed by acid hydrolysis is :
questions.solution: Propyl magnesium bromide (C₃H₇MgBr) is a Grignard reagent. When it reacts with CO₂ (dry ice), the Grignard reagent acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbon of CO₂ to form a magnesium salt of carboxylic acid. Upon acid hydrolysis, this gives butanoic acid (C₃H₇COOH), which is option A. The carbon chain of the Grignard reagent increases by one carbon (from CO₂) to give the acid with one more carbon than the original alkyl group.
questions.topic: Grignard Reagent and Carboxylic Acid Synthesis

questions.text: अम्लीय KMnO₄ सल्फाइट को ऑक्सीकृत कर देता है
questions.text_english: Acidified KMnO₄ oxidises sulphite to
questions.solution: Acidified potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) is a strong oxidising agent. Sulphite ion (SO₃²⁻) has sulphur in +4 oxidation state. Upon oxidation by acidified KMnO₄, the sulphur is oxidised from +4 to +6, yielding sulphate ion (SO₄²⁻). The overall reaction involves the reduction of MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁻ in acidic medium. The other options (thiosulphate, persulphate, SO₂) are not the products of this standard reaction.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में अम्ल सामर्थ्य का सही क्रम कौन सा है ?
questions.text_english: Which is the correct order of acid strength from the following ?
questions.solution: The acid strength depends on the stability of the conjugate base formed after loss of a proton. In phenol (C₆H₅OH), the phenoxide ion (C₆H₅O⁻) is stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring, making phenol more acidic than water and aliphatic alcohols. Water (H₂O) is more acidic than aliphatic alcohols (ROH) because alkyl groups are electron-donating, which destabilises the alkoxide ion (RO⁻) by increasing its electron density, making it a stronger base and the alcohol a weaker acid. Therefore the correct order is C₆H₅OH > H₂O > ROH.

questions.text: अचार बनाने के लिए नमक के सांद्र विलयन में रखा गया कच्चा आम सिकुड़ जाता है, क्योंकि ______
questions.text_english: An unripe mango placed in a concentrated salt solution to prepare pickle, shrivels because _______.

options.A: यह परासरण के कारण जल प्राप्त करता है।
options.B: यह उत्क्रम परासरण के कारण जल खो देता है।
options.C: यह उत्क्रम परासरण के कारण जल प्राप्त करता है।
options.D: यह परासरण के कारण जल खो देता है।

options_english.A: it gains water due to osmosis
options_english.B: it loses water due to reverse osmosis
options_english.C: it gains water due to reverse osmosis
options_english.D: it loses water due to osmosis

questions.solution: The concentrated salt solution outside the mango has a higher solute concentration (lower water potential) compared to the cell sap inside the mango. Water flows from the region of higher water potential (inside the mango cells) to lower water potential (the salt solution) through the semi-permeable cell membranes. This movement of water from inside to outside is osmosis. As water leaves the mango cells, the mango shrivels. Hence, it loses water due to osmosis, which is option D.

questions.text: प्रोपेनामाइड को प्रोपेनेमीन में परिवर्तित करने के लिए सबसे उत्तम अभिकर्मक __________ है।
questions.text_english: The best reagent for converting propanamide into propanamine is _______.

options.C: लाल फॉस्फोरस की उपस्थिति में आयोडीन

options_english.C: iodine in the presence of red phosphorus

questions.solution: To convert propanamide (CH₃CH₂CONH₂) into propanamine (CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂), we need to reduce the amide (C–N bond with C=O) to an amine. LiAlH₄ (lithium aluminium hydride) in dry ether is the best reagent for this reduction as it reduces both the carbonyl and the nitrogen without cleaving the C–N bond, giving the primary amine with the same number of carbons. Br₂/NaOH (Hoffmann bromamide degradation) would give an amine with one fewer carbon (ethanamine). Excess H₂ and iodine/red phosphorus are not appropriate for amide reduction.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन ग्लूकोज़ के विषय में सत्य नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following statements is not true about glucose ?

options.B: HI के साथ गर्म करने पर यह n-हेक्सेन बनाता है।
options.C: यह फ्यूरेनोस रूप में उपस्थित होता है।

options_english.B: On heating with HI it forms n-hexane.
options_english.D: It does not give Schiff’s test.

questions.solution: Glucose is an aldohexose (A is true) with 6 carbon atoms; on heating with HI it undergoes complete reduction to form n-hexane (B is true). The open-chain form of glucose does react with Schiff’s reagent giving a pink colour, making statement D (that it does not give Schiff’s test) debatable, but the clearly false statement is C. Glucose exists predominantly in the pyranose form (a six-membered ring), NOT the furanose form (a five-membered ring). Fructose exists in the furanose form. Hence option C is not true about glucose.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : ग्लाइसीन के अतिरिक्त सभी प्राकृतिक रूप से पाए जाने वाले α-ऐमीनो अम्ल ध्रुवण घूर्णक होते हैं।
कारण (R) : अधिकांश प्राकृतिक रूप से पाए जाने वाले ऐमीनो अम्लों में L-विन्यास होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : All naturally occurring α-amino acids except glycine are optically active.
Reason (R) : Most naturally occurring amino acids have L-configuration.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The Assertion (A) is true: all naturally occurring α-amino acids except glycine have a chiral centre (the α-carbon) and are therefore optically active. The Reason (R) is also true: most naturally occurring amino acids do indeed have L-configuration. However, R does not correctly explain A because optical activity is due to the presence of a chiral centre, not merely because the amino acids have L-configuration. The configuration (L or D) describes the spatial arrangement relative to glyceraldehyde, whereas optical activity requires the presence of an asymmetric carbon. Hence, both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A. The correct answer is (B).

अभिकथन (A) : एथेनॉल का क्वथनांक मेथॉक्सीमेथेन से अधिक होता है।
कारण (R) : एथेनॉल में अंतः अणुक हाइड्रोजन बंध होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The boiling point of ethanol is higher than that of methoxymethane.
Reason (R) : There is intramolecular hydrogen bonding in ethanol.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से।

options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: The Assertion (A) is true: ethanol (b.p. 78°C) has a significantly higher boiling point than methoxymethane/dimethyl ether (b.p. −24°C) due to the presence of strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding in ethanol. However, the Reason (R) is false: ethanol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds (between different ethanol molecules), NOT intramolecular hydrogen bonds (which would be within the same molecule). Intramolecular H-bonding would actually lower the boiling point. Hence Assertion A is correct but Reason R is incorrect, making option C the right answer.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : ऐल्किल हैलाइडों के क्वथनांक निम्न क्रम में घटते हैं : RI > RBr > RCl > RF।
कारण (R) : ऐल्किल क्लोराइड, ब्रोमाइड और आयोडाइड के क्वथनांक तुलनीय आणविक द्रव्यमान वाले हाइड्रोकार्बन की तुलना में काफी अधिक होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The boiling points of alkyl halides decrease in the order : RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
Reason (R) : The boiling points of alkyl chlorides, bromides and iodides are considerably higher than that of the hydrocarbon of comparable molecular mass.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true: the boiling points of alkyl halides decrease in the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF because boiling point increases with increasing molecular mass and polarisability; iodine being the largest and most polarisable halogen leads to the strongest van der Waals interactions and highest boiling point. Reason (R) is also true: alkyl halides have higher boiling points than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular mass because the presence of a halogen atom introduces dipole-dipole interactions in addition to van der Waals forces. However, R does not explain A because A is about the relative order among the halides (which depends on mass and polarisability), while R speaks about halides vs hydrocarbons. Hence both are true but R does not correctly explain A; option B is correct.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₂ तथा [Fe(H₂O)₆]Cl₂ होमोलेप्टिक संकुल के उदाहरण हैं।
कारण (R) : धातु के साथ जुड़े सभी लिगैन्ड एक प्रकार के हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₂ and [Fe(H₂O)₆]Cl₂ are examples of homoleptic complexes.
Reason (R) : All the ligands attached to the metal are the same.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से सही उत्तर चुनिए (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: A homoleptic complex is one in which the metal is coordinated by only one type of ligand. In both [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₂ and [Fe(H₂O)₆]Cl₂, the coordination sphere (inner sphere) contains only water (H₂O) as the ligand — all six ligands around the metal are identical. The Cl⁻ ions are outside the coordination sphere as counter ions. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true. Reason (R) — that all ligands attached to the metal are the same — is also true and correctly explains why these are homoleptic complexes. The correct answer is (A).

questions.text: क्या आप अपेक्षा करते हैं कि प्रोपेनल की तुलना में बेंज़ैल्डिहाइड नाभिकरागी योगज अभिक्रियाओं में अधिक अभिक्रियाशील या कम अभिक्रियाशील होगा ? अपना उत्तर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Would you expect benzaldehyde to be more reactive or less reactive in nucleophilic addition reactions than propanal ? Justify your answer.

key_points: Benzaldehyde is less reactive than propanal in nucleophilic addition reactions.
The carbonyl carbon in benzaldehyde is less electrophilic due to resonance between the benzene ring and the carbonyl group.

In propanal, the alkyl group slightly donates electrons inductively but there is no resonance delocalization onto the carbonyl carbon, making it more electrophilic and hence more reactive towards nucleophiles.

questions.solution: Benzaldehyde is less reactive than propanal in nucleophilic addition reactions. In benzaldehyde, the lone pair electrons of the carbonyl oxygen and the π electrons of the C=O bond are in conjugation with the π system of the benzene ring. This resonance delocalises electron density away from the carbonyl carbon onto the ring, reducing the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon and making it less electrophilic. A less electrophilic carbonyl carbon is less susceptible to attack by a nucleophile. In propanal, only a small inductive effect of the ethyl group operates and there is no such resonance stabilisation; hence the carbonyl carbon remains more electrophilic and more reactive towards nucleophilic addition.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित रासायनिक समीकरण को पूर्ण एवं संतुलित कीजिए :
(a) 8MnO₄⁻ + 3S₂O₃²⁻ + H₂O →
(b) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3Sn²⁺ + 14H⁺ →
questions.text_english:
Complete and balance the following chemical equations :
(a) 8MnO₄⁻ + 3S₂O₃²⁻ + H₂O →
(b) Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3Sn²⁺ + 14H⁺ →

key_points: (a) 8MnO4⁻ + 3S2O3²⁻ + H2O → 8MnO2 + 6SO4²⁻ + 2OH⁻
(b) Cr2O7²⁻ + 3Sn²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3Sn⁴⁺ + 7H2O

questions.solution: For equation (a): Permanganate (MnO₄⁻) is the oxidising agent acting in neutral or basic medium. Mn goes from +7 to +4 (in MnO₂), a gain of 3 electrons per Mn, so 8 Mn atoms gain 24 electrons. Thiosulphate (S₂O₃²⁻) is oxidised to sulphate (SO₄²⁻); each S in S₂O₃²⁻ is +2 and in SO₄²⁻ is +6, a loss of 4 electrons per S, so 3 moles of S₂O₃²⁻ (6 S atoms) lose 24 electrons. The balanced equation is: 8MnO₄⁻ + 3S₂O₃²⁻ + H₂O → 8MnO₂ + 6SO₄²⁻ + 2OH⁻. For equation (b): Dichromate (Cr₂O₇²⁻) acts in acidic medium. Each Cr goes from +6 to +3 (gain of 3e), and 2 Cr atoms gain 6 electrons. Sn goes from +2 to +4 (loss of 2e), so 3 Sn atoms lose 6 electrons. The balanced equation is: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3Sn²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3Sn⁴⁺ + 7H₂O.

sub_questions.solution: Inside a pressure cooker, the steam cannot escape and the pressure builds up above atmospheric pressure. According to the elevation of boiling point principle, an increase in pressure raises the boiling point of water. sub_questions.solution: When the volume of the resulting solution decreases on mixing, it indicates that the intermolecular forces between X and Y molecules are stronger than those in pure X or pure Y. Since the mixing process is exothermic (stronger intermolecular interactions release energy), the temperature of the solution increases after mixing.

questions.text_english: (B) Define Azeotrope. What type of Azeotrope is formed by negative deviation from Raoult’s law ? Give an example.

key_points: Azeotrope: a mixture of two liquids that has a constant boiling point and cannot be separated by simple distillation.
Negative deviation forms a maximum boiling azeotrope.
Example: HNO3 and water (68% HNO3, b.p. 393.5 K).

questions.solution: An azeotrope (or azeotropic mixture) is a binary liquid mixture that has a constant boiling point and composition throughout distillation, meaning the vapour has the same composition as the liquid and the two components cannot be separated by fractional distillation. Negative deviation from Raoult’s law occurs when the intermolecular interactions between unlike molecules (A–B) are stronger than those in pure components (A–A and B–B). This causes a decrease in vapour pressure compared to ideal behaviour, leading to the formation of a maximum boiling azeotrope (the mixture boils at a higher temperature than either pure component). An example is the mixture of nitric acid (HNO₃) and water, which forms a maximum boiling azeotrope at approximately 68% HNO₃ composition with a boiling point of 393.5 K.

निम्नलिखित प्रत्येक अनुक्रम अभिक्रिया में A और B की पहचान कीजिए :
(a) CH₃CH₂Cl →(NaCN) A →(H₂/Ni) B
(b) C₆H₅NH₂ →(NaNO₂/HCl, 0–5°C) A →(C₆H₅NH₂/H⁺) B
questions.text_english:
Identify A and B in each of the following reaction sequence :
(a) CH₃CH₂Cl →(NaCN) A →(H₂/Ni) B
(b) C₆H₅NH₂ →(NaNO₂/HCl, 0–5°C) A →(C₆H₅NH₂/H⁺) B

key_points: (a) A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile/propanenitrile); B = CH3CH2CH2NH2 (propan-1-amine)
(b) A = C6H5N2+Cl- (benzene diazonium chloride); B = C6H5NHC6H5 ... actually diazonium coupling gives azo dye, but here coupling with C6H5NH2/H+ gives C6H5N=NC6H4NH2 (p-aminoazobenzene)

questions.solution: For sequence (a): Chloroethane (CH₃CH₂Cl) reacts with NaCN in an SN2 reaction, where CN⁻ acts as nucleophile, replacing Cl⁻ to give CH₃CH₂CN (propanenitrile), so A = CH₃CH₂CN. Reduction of this nitrile with H₂/Ni (catalytic hydrogenation) converts –C≡N to –CH₂NH₂, giving propan-1-amine (CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂), so B = CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂. For sequence (b): Aniline (C₆H₅NH₂) reacts with NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5°C (diazotisation) to form benzene diazonium chloride (C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻), so A = C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻. This diazonium salt couples with aniline (C₆H₅NH₂) in weakly acidic medium (coupling reaction) to form p-aminoazobenzene (an azo dye), so B = p-H₂N–C₆H₄–N=N–C₆H₅.

(b) Lactose on hydrolysis gives D-galactose and D-glucose.

questions.solution: Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by the combination of one molecule of D-glucose and one molecule of D-fructose joined by a glycosidic linkage involving the anomeric carbons of both monosaccharides. On hydrolysis (with dilute acid or the enzyme sucrase/invertase), sucrose gives D-glucose and D-fructose. Lactose is a disaccharide found in milk, formed by the combination of D-galactose and D-glucose linked by a β-1,4-glycosidic bond. On hydrolysis (with dilute acid or the enzyme lactase), lactose gives D-galactose and D-glucose.

questions.text: 298 K पर जल में CO₂ गैस की जल में विलेयता के लिए हेनरी स्थिरांक का मान 1.67 × 10⁸ Pa है। समान ताप पर 500 ml सोडा जल 2.53 × 10⁵ Pa दाब पर बंद किया गया। सोडा जल में घुली हुई CO₂ के मोलों की गणना कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Henry’s law constant for CO₂ in water is 1.67 × 10⁸ Pa at 298 K. Calculate the number of moles of CO₂ in 500 ml of soda water when packed under 2.53 × 10⁵ Pa at the same temperature.

key_points: Apply Henry’s law: p = KH × x (mole fraction)
Moles of water in 500 mL = 500/18 ≈ 27.78 mol
Moles of CO2 = x × n(water) ≈ 0.042 mol

questions.solution:
Using Henry’s law: p(CO₂) = K_H × x(CO₂), where x(CO₂) is the mole fraction of CO₂.
x(CO₂) = p / K_H = (2.53 × 10⁵) / (1.67 × 10⁸) = 1.515 × 10⁻³.
Mass of 500 mL of water = 500 g (assuming density = 1 g/mL).
Moles of water = 500 / 18 = 27.78 mol.
Since x(CO₂) = n(CO₂) / [n(CO₂) + n(H₂O)], and since x(CO₂) is very small, n(CO₂) + n(H₂O) ≈ n(H₂O) = 27.78 mol.
Therefore, n(CO₂) = x(CO₂) × n(H₂O) = 1.515 × 10⁻³ × 27.78 = 0.0421 mol ≈ 0.042 mol.
Hence, the number of moles of CO₂ dissolved in 500 mL of soda water is approximately 0.042 mol.

questions.text:
अभिक्रिया के ΔᵣG° और log Kᴄ की गणना कीजिए।
2Cr(s) + 3Cd²⁺(aq) → 2Cr³⁺(aq) + 3Cd(s)
दिया गया है : E°ᴄr³⁺/Cr = −0.74 V
E°ᴄd²⁺/Cd = −0.40 V
[R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.text_english:
Calculate ΔᵣG° and log K_C of the reaction.
2Cr(s) + 3Cd²⁺(aq) → 2Cr³⁺(aq) + 3Cd(s)
Given E°ᴄr³⁺/Cr = −0.74 V
E°ᴄd²⁺/Cd = −0.40 V
[R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]

key_points: E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = -0.40 - (-0.74) = +0.34 V
n = 6 (3 Cd each gaining 2e, 2 Cr each losing 3e)

questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify cathode and anode. Cd²⁺/Cd has higher (less negative) E° = −0.40 V, so Cd²⁺ is reduced (cathode). Cr/Cr³⁺ with E° = −0.74 V is oxidised (anode).
Step 2: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = (−0.40) − (−0.74) = +0.34 V.
Step 3: Number of electrons transferred (n): Each Cr loses 3 electrons (2 Cr atoms → 6e⁻) and each Cd²⁺ gains 2 electrons (3 Cd²⁺ → 6e⁻). So n = 6.
Step 4: ΔᵣG° = −nFE° = −(6)(96500)(0.34) = −196,860 J mol⁻¹ ≈ −196.86 kJ mol⁻¹.
Step 5: log K_C = nE° / (2.303RT/F) = nE° / (0.0591) [at 298 K] = (6 × 0.34) / 0.0591 = 2.04 / 0.0591 ≈ 34.52.

questions.text:
जब ताप 293 K से 313 K तक बदलता है तो अभिक्रिया की दर चौगुनी हो जाती है। अभिक्रिया की सक्रियण ऊर्जा की गणना कीजिए यह मानते हुए कि यह ताप के साथ नहीं बदलती है।
[दिया है : log 4 = 0.602, log 2 = 0.301, R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹]
questions.text_english:
The rate of a reaction quadruples when the temperature changes from 293 K to 313 K. Calculate the energy of activation of the reaction assuming that it does not change with temperature.
[Given : log 4 = 0.602, log 2 = 0.301, R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹]

key_points: Use Arrhenius equation: log(k2/k1) = Ea/(2.303R) × (T2-T1)/(T1T2)
Ea ≈ 52,897 J/mol ≈ 52.9 kJ/mol

questions.solution:
Using the Arrhenius equation in its two-temperature form:
log(k₂/k₁) = (Ea / 2.303R) × [(T₂ − T₁) / (T₁ × T₂)]
Here k₂/k₁ = 4, T₁ = 293 K, T₂ = 313 K, R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
log(4) = 0.602.
T₁ × T₂ = 293 × 313 = 91,709 K².
T₂ − T₁ = 20 K.
0.602 = Ea / (2.303 × 8.314) × (20 / 91709)
Ea = 0.602 × 2.303 × 8.314 × (91709 / 20)
Ea = 0.602 × 2.303 × 8.314 × 4585.45
Ea = 0.602 × 87,835.5
Ea ≈ 52,897 J mol⁻¹ ≈ 52.9 kJ mol⁻¹.
Therefore, the energy of activation of the reaction is approximately 52.9 kJ mol⁻¹.

(a) 2-chloro-1-ethylbenzene + Br₂, heat
(b) 1-methylcyclohexene + HBr
(c) benzyl alcohol (HO-H₂C-C₆H₅) + HCl, heat
questions.text_english:
(A) Draw the structure of the major monohalo product for each of the following reaction :
(a) 2-chloro-1-ethylbenzene treated with Br₂ and Heat
(b) 1-methylcyclohexene + HBr
(c) benzyl alcohol (HO-H₂C-C₆H₅) + HCl, Heat

key_points: (a) Br replaces a benzylic H on the -CH2CH3 side chain at the benzylic position: 2-chloro-1-(1-bromoethyl)benzene
(b) HBr adds as per Markovnikov's rule: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane
(c) The OH group is replaced by Cl (Lucas reaction): benzyl chloride (C6H5CH2Cl)

questions.solution: For reaction (a): The reaction of an alkylbenzene with Br₂ under heat (radical conditions) results in free radical halogenation at the benzylic position because the benzylic radical is stabilised by resonance. In 2-chloro-1-ethylbenzene, the benzylic carbon of the –CH₂CH₃ group (the α-carbon) is brominated to give 2-chloro-1-(1-bromoethyl)benzene as the major product. For reaction (b): Addition of HBr to 1-methylcyclohexene follows Markovnikov’s rule. The proton adds to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms (the unsubstituted ring carbon) and Br⁻ adds to the tertiary carbon (bearing the methyl group), giving 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane as the major product. For reaction (c): Benzyl alcohol reacts with HCl under heat in an SN1 reaction. The benzylic carbocation (C₆H₅CH₂⁺) formed is highly stable due to resonance with the benzene ring. Cl⁻ attacks the carbocation to give benzyl chloride (C₆H₅CH₂Cl) as the major product.

questions.text_english:
(B) How do you convert :
(a) Chlorobenzene to biphenyl
(b) Propene to 1-Iodopropane
(c) 2-bromobutane to but-2-ene.

key_points: (a) Chlorobenzene to biphenyl via Ullmann reaction (2C6H5Cl + 2Na/dry ether → C6H5-C6H5 + 2NaCl) or via Grignard reagent coupling.
(b) Propene + HI → 2-iodopropane (Markovnikov), then 2-iodopropane + NaI/acetone or propene + HBr then treat to get 1-iodopropane via anti-Markovnikov with peroxide then substitution.
(c) 2-bromobutane + alc. KOH → but-2-ene (dehydrohalogenation/elimination).

questions.solution: For conversion (a): Chlorobenzene is converted to biphenyl using the Ullmann coupling reaction. Two moles of chlorobenzene are treated with sodium metal in dry ether (or copper powder at high temperature): 2C₆H₅Cl + 2Na → C₆H₅–C₆H₅ (biphenyl) + 2NaCl. For conversion (b): Propene is converted to 1-iodopropane by first adding HBr in the presence of peroxide (anti-Markovnikov addition) to give 1-bromopropane, and then treating with NaI in acetone (Finkelstein reaction) to replace Br with I: CH₃CH=CH₂ →(HBr/peroxide) CH₃CH₂CH₂Br →(NaI/acetone) CH₃CH₂CH₂I. For conversion (c): 2-Bromobutane is converted to but-2-ene by heating with alcoholic KOH (dehydrohalogenation/β-elimination): CH₃CHBrCH₂CH₃ + KOH(alc.) → CH₃CH=CHCH₃ + KBr + H₂O.

3d संक्रमण श्रेणी के तत्व इस प्रकार दिए गए हैं:
Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn
निम्नलिखित का उत्तर दीजिए:
(a) कॉपर का E°ₘ²⁺/ₘ मान असाधारण रूप से धनात्मक है, क्यों ?
(b) कौन सा तत्व +2 ऑक्सीकरण अवस्था में एक प्रबल अपचायक है और क्यों ?
(c) Zn²⁺ लवण रंगहीन होते हैं, क्यों ?
questions.text_english:
The elements of 3d transition series are given as :
Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn
Answer the following :
(a) Copper has exceptionally positive E°ₘ²⁺/ₘ value, why ?
(b) Which element is a strong reducing agent in +2 oxidation state and why ?
(c) Zn²⁺ salts are colourless. Why ?

key_points: (a) Copper has high heat of atomisation and low hydration enthalpy, making it difficult to oxidise; hence its reduction potential is exceptionally high (positive).
(b) Ti²⁺ (titanium in +2 state) is a strong reducing agent because Ti²⁺ has a strong tendency to be oxidised to Ti⁴⁺, acquiring the stable d⁰ configuration.
(c) Zn²⁺ has a d¹⁰ configuration with no unpaired electrons; no d-d transitions are possible, so its salts are colourless.

questions.solution: For part (a): Copper has an exceptionally high (positive) E° value for Cu²⁺/Cu because the sum of first and second ionisation enthalpies of Cu is very high, and the hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ is relatively low compared to other transition metals. The energy required to convert Cu(s) to Cu²⁺(aq) is not adequately compensated by the hydration enthalpy, making Cu difficult to oxidise and its reduction potential therefore very positive. For part (b): Ti²⁺ (titanium in +2 oxidation state) is a strong reducing agent because Ti²⁺ readily loses two more electrons to reach Ti⁴⁺, which has the stable d⁰ electronic configuration. This strong tendency to be further oxidised makes Ti²⁺ a powerful reducing agent. For part (c): Zn²⁺ has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰, i.e., a completely filled d-subshell. Since all d orbitals are fully occupied, there are no unpaired d electrons and no possibility of d–d electronic transitions. In the absence of such transitions, no visible light is absorbed, and therefore Zn²⁺ salts are colourless.

(a) निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को उनके क्वथनांक के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित करें:
(CH₃)₂NH, CH₃CH₂NH₂, CH₃CH₂OH

(i) ऐरोमैटिक प्राथमिक ऐमीनों को गैब्रिएल थैलिमाइड संश्लेषण से नहीं बनाया जा सकता।
(ii) एमाइड, ऐमीनों की तुलना में कम क्षारकीय होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
(a) Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their boiling point :
(CH₃)₂NH, CH₃CH₂NH₂, CH₃CH₂OH.
(b) Give plausible explanation for each of the following :
(i) Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis.
(ii) Amides are less basic than amines.

key_points: (a) (CH3)2NH < CH3CH2NH2 < CH3CH2OH
(b)(i) Gabriel synthesis requires alkyl halides; aryl halides are not reactive enough for nucleophilic substitution with phthalimide anion.
(b)(ii) In amides, the lone pair on N is delocalised into the C=O group by resonance, making it less available for protonation.

questions.solution: For part (a): The boiling points depend on hydrogen bonding ability. Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) has the highest boiling point due to the strong intermolecular O–H···O hydrogen bonds. Ethanamine (CH₃CH₂NH₂) forms N–H···N hydrogen bonds, which are weaker than O–H bonds, so its boiling point is lower than ethanol. Dimethylamine ((CH₃)₂NH) has only one N–H group and hence less hydrogen bonding capacity; moreover it is a secondary amine, so its boiling point is the lowest among the three. The order of increasing boiling point is: (CH₃)₂NH < CH₃CH₂NH₂ < CH₃CH₂OH. For part (b)(i): Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves treating potassium phthalimide with an alkyl halide in an SN2 reaction. Aryl halides are very poor substrates for SN2 reactions because the sp²-hybridised carbon of the aryl ring is less susceptible to back-side nucleophilic attack, and the negative charge cannot be accommodated at an sp² carbon in the transition state. Hence aromatic primary amines (like aniline) cannot be prepared by this method. For part (b)(ii): In amides, the nitrogen lone pair is involved in resonance with the adjacent carbonyl group (C=O), forming a partial C–N double bond. This delocalisation reduces the electron density on nitrogen, making the lone pair much less available for accepting a proton. Therefore, amides are significantly less basic than amines, where the lone pair on nitrogen is freely available for protonation.
questions.topic: Boiling Points of Amines; Gabriel Synthesis; Basicity of Amides

निम्नलिखित शब्दों को परिभाषित करें:

(b) न्यूक्लियोटाइड
(c) आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल
questions.text_english:
Define the following terms :
(a) Native protein
(b) Nucleotide
(c) Essential amino acid

key_points: (a) Native protein: a protein in its naturally occurring, biologically active three-dimensional conformation, maintained by non-covalent interactions.
(b) Nucleotide: the monomer unit of nucleic acids, consisting of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group.
(c) Essential amino acid: an amino acid that cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained from the diet.

questions.solution: A native protein is a protein in its naturally occurring biological state, having a specific and unique three-dimensional structure (its native conformation) that is essential for its biological activity. This structure is maintained by a combination of non-covalent interactions such as hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, ionic interactions, and van der Waals forces. Denaturation disrupts this structure. A nucleotide is the basic structural unit (monomer) of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA). It consists of three components joined together: a nitrogenous base (a purine such as adenine or guanine, or a pyrimidine such as cytosine, thymine, or uracil), a pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA), and a phosphate group. An essential amino acid is an amino acid that the human body cannot synthesise on its own in adequate quantities and which must therefore be supplied through the diet. Examples include lysine, leucine, isoleucine, threonine, methionine, valine, phenylalanine, and tryptophan.

questions.text: रासायनिक अभिक्रिया का वेग या तो प्रति इकाई समय में अभिकारक की सांद्रता में कमी या उत्पाद की सांद्रता में वृद्धि के रूप में व्यक्त किया जाता है। अभिक्रिया का वेग अभिकारकों की प्रकृति, अभिकारकों की सांद्रता, तापमान, उत्प्रेरक की उपस्थिति, अभिकारकों के पृष्ठीय क्षेत्रफल और प्रकाश की उपस्थिति पर निर्भर करता है। अभिक्रिया का वेग अभिकारक की सांद्रता से सीधे संबंधित होता है। वेग नियम बताता है कि अभिक्रिया का वेग सांद्रता पदों पर निर्भर करता है जिस पर अभिक्रिया का वेग वास्तव में निर्भर करता है, जैसा कि प्रयोगात्मक रूप से देखा गया है। वेग नियम अभिव्यक्ति में अभिकारकों की सांद्रता की घातों के योग को अभिक्रिया की कोटि कहा जाता है जबकि एक प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया में भाग लेने वाली स्पीशीज़ की संख्या जो रासायनिक अभिक्रिया सम्पन्न करने के लिए एक साथ संघट्ट करती है, अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता कहलाती है।
questions.text_english: The rate of a chemical reaction is expressed either in terms of decrease in the concentration of reactants or increase in the concentration of a product per unit time. Rate of the reaction depends upon the nature of reactants, concentration of reactants, temperature, presence of catalyst, surface area of the reactants and presence of light. Rate of reaction is directly related to the concentration of reactant. Rate law states that the rate of reaction depends upon the concentration terms on which the rate of reaction actually depends, as observed experimentally. The sum of powers of the concentration of the reactants in the Rate law expression is called order of reaction while the number of reacting species taking part in an elementary reaction which must collide simultaneously in order to bring about a chemical reaction is called molecularity of the reaction.

sub_questions.text: (a)(i) वेग निर्धारक पद क्या है ? (ii) जटिल अभिक्रिया को परिभाषित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a)(i) What is a rate determining step ? (ii) Define complex reaction.

key_points: Rate determining step: the slowest step in a multi-step reaction mechanism that controls the overall rate of the reaction.
Complex reaction: a reaction that proceeds through more than one elementary step (i.e., has a multi-step mechanism).

sub_questions.solution: The rate determining step is the slowest step in a sequence of elementary reactions making up a complex reaction mechanism. Since it is the slowest, it acts as a bottleneck and controls the overall rate of the reaction; the overall rate of the reaction cannot exceed the rate of this step. A complex reaction (also called a multi-step reaction) is a reaction that does not proceed in a single elementary step but instead occurs through a series of two or more elementary steps (each with its own transition state), with the overall equation being the sum of all these elementary steps.

sub_questions.text: (b) वेग स्थिरांक पर ताप का क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) What is the effect of temperature on the rate constant of a reaction ?

key_points: Rate constant increases with increase in temperature, approximately doubling for every 10°C rise, as described by the Arrhenius equation k = Ae^(-Ea/RT).

sub_questions.solution: The rate constant (k) of a reaction increases with an increase in temperature. According to the Arrhenius equation, k = A·e^(−Ea/RT), where A is the pre-exponential factor, Ea is the activation energy, R is the gas constant, and T is the absolute temperature. As temperature increases, a greater fraction of molecules have kinetic energy equal to or greater than the activation energy, leading to more successful collisions and a higher rate constant. As a rule of thumb, the rate approximately doubles for every 10°C rise in temperature.

sub_questions.text: (b) [OR] आण्विकता केवल प्राथमिक अभिक्रियाओं के लिए ही क्यों लागू होती है जबकि कोटि प्राथमिक और जटिल अभिक्रिया दोनों के लिए लागू होती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) [OR] Why is molecularity applicable only for elementary reactions whereas order is applicable for elementary as well as complex reactions ?

key_points: Molecularity is a theoretical concept defined for a single elementary step; complex reactions have no single collision event. Order is an experimentally determined quantity applicable to any reaction.

sub_questions.solution: Molecularity is defined as the number of reacting species (atoms, molecules, or ions) that must simultaneously collide in a single elementary step to bring about that step. It is a theoretical concept applicable only to elementary reactions because each elementary step involves a well-defined collision event. Complex reactions consist of multiple elementary steps, and there is no single collision event for the overall reaction; hence molecularity cannot be defined for complex reactions. In contrast, the order of reaction is determined experimentally from the rate law expression and represents the sum of the exponents of concentration terms. It can be determined for any reaction (elementary or complex) by experiment, and it may even be a fraction or zero.

sub_questions.text: (c) अणु X का Y में रूपांतरण द्वितीय कोटि की बलगतिकी के अनुरूप होता है। यदि X की सांद्रता तीन गुनी कर दी जाए तो Y के निर्माण होने के वेग पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ेगा ?
sub_questions.text_english: (c) The conversion of molecule X to Y follows second order kinetics. If concentration of X is increased 3 times, how will it affect the rate of formation of Y ?

key_points: Rate will increase 9 times (3² = 9) because for second order kinetics, rate ∝ [X]².

sub_questions.solution: For a second order reaction, the rate law is: Rate = k[X]². If the concentration of X is increased 3 times (i.e., [X] becomes 3[X]), the new rate = k(3[X])² = 9k[X]² = 9 × original rate. Therefore, when the concentration of X is tripled, the rate of formation of Y increases 9 times.

questions.text: बेन्जीन वलय से जुड़े OH समूह के प्रबल सक्रियण प्रभाव के कारण फ़ीनॉल आसानी से इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रियाएँ देते हैं। चूँकि OH समूह o– और p– स्थितियों पर इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व को अधिक बढ़ाता है, इसलिए OH समूह ऑर्थो और पैरा निर्देशक होता है। राइमर–टीमन इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के उदाहरण में से एक है। जिसके द्वारा फ़ीनॉल की ऐरोमैटिक वलय में हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह की ऑर्थो स्थिति पर एल्डिहाइड समूह प्रवेश कर जाता है। यह एक सामान्य विधि है जो फ़ीनॉलों के ऑर्थो फार्मिलेशन के लिए प्रयुक्त की जाती है।
questions.text_english: Phenols undergo electrophilic substitution reactions readily due to the strong activating effect of OH group attached to the benzene ring. Since, the OH group increases the electron density more to o– and p– positions therefore OH group is ortho, para-directing. Reimer-Tiemann reaction is one of the examples of aldehyde group being introduced on the aromatic ring of phenol, ortho to the hydroxyl group. This is a general method used for the ortho-formylation of phenols.

sub_questions.text: (a) क्या होता है जब फ़ीनॉल निम्न से अभिक्रिया करता है ? (i) Br₂/CS₂ (ii) सांद्र HNO₃
sub_questions.text_english: (a) What happens when phenol reacts with (i) Br₂/CS₂ (ii) Conc. HNO₃

key_points: (i) Phenol + Br2/CS2 (non-polar solvent, low temperature) gives a mixture of o-bromophenol and p-bromophenol (monosubstitution due to dilute/non-polar conditions).
(ii) Phenol + conc. HNO3 gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).

sub_questions.solution: When phenol reacts with Br₂ in carbon disulphide (CS₂, a non-polar solvent) at low temperature, electrophilic aromatic substitution takes place at the ortho and para positions (since –OH is an ortho-para director). A mixture of o-bromophenol and p-bromophenol is obtained as monohalogenation products. When phenol is treated with concentrated nitric acid, nitration occurs at all three available ortho and para positions. Both ortho positions (2 and 6) and the para position (4) become substituted with –NO₂ groups, giving 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, also known as picric acid.

sub_questions.text: (b) फ़ीनॉल का प्रोटॉनन आसानी से क्यों नहीं होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Why phenol does not undergo protonation readily ?

key_points: The lone pair on the oxygen of phenol is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance, reducing its availability to accept a proton.

sub_questions.solution: In phenol, the lone pair of electrons on the oxygen atom is in conjugation with the π-electron system of the benzene ring. Due to resonance, this lone pair is delocalised over the ring, making it less available (less basic) for accepting a proton. As a result, the oxygen of phenol is less readily protonated compared to, say, aliphatic alcohols where no such resonance delocalisation of the oxygen lone pair occurs.

sub_questions.text: (c) कौन सा एक प्रबल अम्ल है : फ़ीनॉल अथवा क्रीसॉल ? कारण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Which is a stronger acid – phenol or cresol ? Give reason.

key_points: Phenol is a stronger acid than cresol because the methyl group in cresol is electron-donating, which destabilises the phenoxide ion and decreases acidity.

sub_questions.solution: Phenol is a stronger acid than cresol. Cresol has a methyl group (–CH₃) attached to the benzene ring. The methyl group is electron-donating by the +I inductive effect, which increases the electron density on the phenoxide ion (cresoxide ion) formed after deprotonation. A higher electron density on the negative oxygen makes the conjugate base less stable (more basic), which means it is harder to lose the proton, and hence cresol is a weaker acid than phenol.

sub_questions.text: (c) [अथवा] राइमर–टीमन अभिक्रिया में बनने वाले उत्पाद का IUPAC नाम लिखें।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) [OR] Write the IUPAC name of the product formed in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

key_points: 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde)

sub_questions.solution: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl₃) and aqueous sodium hydroxide. The dichlorocarbene intermediate (:CCl₂) generated in situ attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ion, and after hydrolysis, an aldehyde group (–CHO) is introduced ortho to the hydroxyl group. The product is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde, commonly known as salicylaldehyde. Its IUPAC name is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde.

questions.text:
(A)(a) निम्नलिखित रूपांतरण करें:
(i) एथेनल से ब्यूट-2-ईनैल
(ii) प्रोपेनोइक अम्ल से एथेन
(b) आण्विक सूत्र C₅H₁₀ वाला एक एल्कीन A ओज़ोनी अपघटन पर दो यौगिकों B और C का मिश्रण देता है। यौगिक B धनात्मक फेलिंग परीक्षण देता है और आयोडीन और NaOH विलयन के साथ भी अभिक्रिया करता है। यौगिक C फेलिंग परीक्षण नहीं देता है लेकिन आयोडोफार्म बनाता है। यौगिक A, B और C की पहचान कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(A)(a) Carry out the following conversions :
(i) Ethanal to But-2-enal
(ii) Propanoic acid to ethane
(b) An alkene A with molecular formula C₅H₁₀ on ozonolysis gives a mixture of two compounds B and C. Compound B gives positive Fehling test and also reacts with iodine and NaOH solution. Compound C does not give Fehling solution test but forms iodoform. Identify the compounds A, B and C.

key_points: (a)(i) Ethanal to but-2-enal: aldol condensation of two molecules of ethanal using dilute NaOH to give aldol (3-hydroxybutanal), followed by dehydration to but-2-enal.
(a)(ii) Propanoic acid to ethane: convert to propanoic acid salt, then Kolbe electrolysis OR via RCOONa + NaOH with CaO (soda lime) decarboxylation to give ethane.

(b) B gives positive Fehling test (aldehyde) and iodoform test (CH3CHO or methyl ketone), so B = CH3CHO (ethanal). C gives iodoform (CH3CO-) but no Fehling test, so C = CH3COCH3 (propanone/acetone). A (C5H10) on ozonolysis gives CH3CHO + CH3COCH3, so A = CH3CH=C(CH3)2 (2-methylbut-2-ene).

questions.solution: For conversion (a)(i): Ethanal (CH₃CHO) is converted to but-2-enal (CH₃CH=CHCHO) by aldol condensation. Two molecules of ethanal react in the presence of dilute NaOH to form 3-hydroxybutanal (the aldol product). On heating, this undergoes dehydration to give but-2-enal (crotonaldehyde): 2CH₃CHO →(dilute NaOH) CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO →(–H₂O, heat) CH₃CH=CHCHO. For conversion (a)(ii): Propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH) is converted to ethane by decarboxylation. Sodium propanoate (CH₃CH₂COONa) is fused with excess soda lime (NaOH/CaO mixture) to remove the –COOH group as CO₂: CH₃CH₂COONa + NaOH →(CaO, heat) CH₃CH₃ (ethane) + Na₂CO₃. For part (b): Compound B gives a positive Fehling test (indicating an aldehyde function) and also gives the iodoform test (indicating the –COCH₃ or –CH(OH)CH₃ group). The compound satisfying both is ethanal (CH₃CHO), so B = CH₃CHO. Compound C gives the iodoform test (indicating a methyl ketone group) but does not give the Fehling test (so it is not an aldehyde). This corresponds to propanone (CH₃COCH₃), so C = CH₃COCH₃. For compound A: ozonolysis of A gives B (CH₃CHO) and C (CH₃COCH₃). Reconnecting these fragments at the site of ozonolysis (–C=C–), we get CH₃CH=C(CH₃)CH₃, which is 2-methylbut-2-ene with molecular formula C₅H₁₀. Therefore A = 2-methylbut-2-ene (CH₃CH=C(CH₃)₂).
questions.topic: Aldol Condensation; Decarboxylation; Ozonolysis; Iodoform Test

questions.text: (B) एक कार्बनिक यौगिक (A) (आण्विक सूत्र C₈H₁₆O₂) को तनु सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल के साथ जल अपघटन करके कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल (B) और एल्कोहॉल (C) प्राप्त हुआ। (C) का क्रोमिक अम्ल के साथ ऑक्सीकरण करने पर (B) बनता है। निर्जलीकरण पर (C) ब्यूट-1-ईन देता है। (A), (B) और (C) को पहचानिए तथा सम्मिलित अभिक्रियाओं के लिए रासायनिक समीकरण लिखिए।
questions.text_english: (B) An organic compound (A) (molecular formula C₈H₁₆O₂) was hydrolysed with dilute sulphuric acid to get a carboxylic acid (B) and an alcohol (C). Oxidation of (C) with chromic acid produced (B). (C) on dehydration gives But-1-ene. Identify (A), (B) and (C) and write chemical equations for the reactions involved.

key_points: C dehydrates to but-1-ene, so C is butan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH).
Oxidation of C (butan-1-ol) with chromic acid gives B = butanoic acid (CH3CH2CH2COOH).
A (C8H16O2) is an ester that hydrolyses to B and C: A = butyl butanoate (CH3CH2CH2COOCH2CH2CH2CH3).

questions.solution: Step 1 – Identify C: Compound C on dehydration gives but-1-ene (CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂). The alcohol that dehydrates to give but-1-ene (with the double bond at C1–C2) is butan-1-ol, so C = CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH. Step 2 – Identify B: Oxidation of butan-1-ol (a primary alcohol) with chromic acid gives the corresponding carboxylic acid, so B = butanoic acid (CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH). Step 3 – Identify A: Compound A (molecular formula C₈H₁₆O₂) on hydrolysis with dilute H₂SO₄ gives B (butanoic acid) and C (butan-1-ol). A is therefore an ester formed from butanoic acid and butan-1-ol, i.e., butyl butanoate: CH₃CH₂CH₂COO–CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃. Chemical equations: (1) Hydrolysis: CH₃(CH₂)₂COOCH₂(CH₂)₂CH₃ + H₂O →(dil. H₂SO₄) CH₃(CH₂)₂COOH + CH₃(CH₂)₂CH₂OH. (2) Oxidation: CH₃(CH₂)₂CH₂OH →(CrO₃/H₂SO₄) CH₃(CH₂)₂COOH. (3) Dehydration: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH →(H₂SO₄, heat) CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂ + H₂O.
questions.topic: Identification of Organic Compounds from Properties

questions.text:
(A) निम्नलिखित संकुल आयनों के लिए संकरण का प्रकार, आकार और चुंबकीय गुण की व्याख्या कीजिए:
(a) [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺
(b) [NiCl₄]²⁻
(परमाणु संख्या : Fe = 26, Ni = 28)
questions.text_english:
(A) In the following complex ions, explain the type of hybridisation, shape and magnetic property :
(a) [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺
(b) [NiCl₄]²⁻
(At. Nos. : Fe = 26, Ni = 28)

key_points: [Fe(H2O)6]2+: Fe is in +2 state, configuration [Ar]3d6. H2O is a weak field ligand so no pairing, 4 unpaired electrons. sp3d2 hybridisation (outer orbital), octahedral shape, paramagnetic.
[NiCl4]2-: Ni is in +2 state, configuration [Ar]3d8. Cl- is weak field, no pairing, 2 unpaired electrons. sp3 hybridisation, tetrahedral shape, paramagnetic.

questions.solution: For [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺: Iron is in the +2 oxidation state. Fe atomic number is 26, so Fe²⁺ has the configuration [Ar] 3d⁶. Water (H₂O) is a weak field ligand and does not cause pairing of electrons. In Fe²⁺ with 3d⁶, the six 3d electrons occupy the five 3d orbitals with 4 unpaired electrons. The complex uses outer orbital hybridisation: one 4s, three 4p, and two 4d orbitals combine to give six sp³d² hybrid orbitals, giving an octahedral shape. The presence of 4 unpaired electrons makes the complex paramagnetic. For [NiCl₄]²⁻: Nickel is in the +2 oxidation state. Ni atomic number is 28, so Ni²⁺ has configuration [Ar] 3d⁸. Chloride (Cl⁻) is a weak field ligand, so it does not cause pairing of electrons. The 3d⁸ configuration has 2 unpaired electrons. Four Cl⁻ ligands coordinate using sp³ hybridisation of the Ni²⁺ orbitals (one 4s and three 4p). The shape is tetrahedral. The presence of 2 unpaired electrons makes the complex paramagnetic.
questions.topic: Hybridisation, Shape, and Magnetic Properties of Complexes

questions.text:
(B)(a) निम्नलिखित के IUPAC नाम लिखिए:
(i) [Co(H₂O)(CN)(en)₂]²⁺
(ii) [PtCl₄]²⁻
(iii) [Cr(NH₃)₄Cl(ONO)]⁺
(b) स्पेक्ट्रोरासायनिक श्रेणी क्या है ? प्रबल क्षेत्र लिगैन्ड तथा दुर्बल क्षेत्र लिगैन्ड में अंतर लिखिए।
questions.text_english:
(B)(a) Write IUPAC names of the following :
(i) [Co(H₂O)(CN)(en)₂]²⁺
(ii) [PtCl₄]²⁻
(iii) [Cr(NH₃)₄Cl(ONO)]⁺
(b) What is spectrochemical series ? Write the difference between a strong field ligand and a weak field ligand.

key_points: (a)(i) Aquacyanobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) ion
(a)(ii) Tetrachloridoplatinate(II) ion
(a)(iii) Tetraamminechloridonitrito-O-chromium(III) ion

(b) Spectrochemical series: arrangement of ligands in increasing order of crystal field splitting (Δ). Strong field ligands: cause large Δ, force electron pairing, give low-spin complexes (e.g. CN-, CO). Weak field ligands: cause small Δ, do not force pairing, give high-spin complexes (e.g. Cl-, F-, H2O).

questions.solution: For part (a)(i): The complex [Co(H₂O)(CN)(en)₂]²⁺ contains Co as the central metal. The ligands are one aqua (H₂O), one cyano (CN⁻), and two ethane-1,2-diamine (en) groups. Co oxidation state = +3 (since charge on complex = +2 = x + 0 − 1 + 0; checking: x − 1 = +2, so x = +3). Naming alphabetically: aqua, cyano, bis(ethane-1,2-diamine), then the metal with oxidation state. IUPAC name: aquacyanobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) ion. For part (a)(ii): [PtCl₄]²⁻ contains Pt in +2 state (x − 4 = −2, so x = +2). This is an anionic complex, so the metal is named with the ‘-ate’ suffix. IUPAC name: tetrachloridoplatinate(II) ion. For part (a)(iii): [Cr(NH₃)₄Cl(ONO)]⁺ contains 4 ammine, 1 chlorido, and 1 nitrito-O (ONO⁻, bound through oxygen) ligands. Cr oxidation state: x + 0 − 1 − 1 = +1, so x = +3. IUPAC name: tetraamminechloridonitrito-κO-chromium(III) ion. For part (b): The spectrochemical series is the arrangement of ligands in increasing order of their ability to cause crystal field splitting (Δ) of the d-orbitals of the central metal ion: I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < en < CO ≈ CN⁻. Strong field ligands (such as CN⁻ and CO) cause a large crystal field splitting; when Δ exceeds the pairing energy, electrons are forced to pair in the lower energy orbitals, forming low-spin complexes with fewer unpaired electrons and weaker paramagnetism or diamagnetism. Weak field ligands (such as Cl⁻, Br⁻, and F⁻) cause a small crystal field splitting; the pairing energy exceeds Δ, so electrons remain unpaired, forming high-spin complexes with more unpaired electrons and stronger paramagnetism.
questions.topic: IUPAC Nomenclature; Spectrochemical Series; Strong and Weak Field Ligands

questions.text:
(A)(a) निम्नलिखित के लिए सेल अभिक्रिया लिखिए तथा 298 K पर सेल का e.m.f. परिकलित कीजिए:
Sn(s) | Sn²⁺ (0.004 M) || H⁺ (0.02 M) | H₂(g) (1 Bar) | Pt(s)
दिया गया है : E°ₘn²⁺/ₘn = –0.14 V, E°_H⁺|H₂(g),Pt = 0.00 V
(b) निम्नलिखित के कारण बताइए:
(i) E° मानों के आधार पर, O₂ गैस एनोड पर मुक्त होनी चाहिए, लेकिन जलीय NaCl के विद्युत अपघटन में Cl₂ गैस मुक्त होती है।
(ii) तनुकरण पर CH₃COOH की चालकता कम हो जाती है।
questions.text_english:
(A)(a) Write the cell reaction and calculate the e.m.f. of the following cell at 298 K :
Sn(s) | Sn²⁺ (0.004 M) || H⁺ (0.02 M) | H₂(g) (1 Bar) | Pt(s)
(Given : E°ₘn²⁺/Sn = −0.14 V, E°H⁺|H₂(g),Pt = 0.00 V)
(b) Account for the following ;
(i) On the basis of E° values, O₂ gas should be liberated at anode but it is Cl₂ gas which is liberated in the electrolysis of aqueous NaCl.
(ii) Conductivity of CH₃COOH decreases on dilution.

key_points: (b)(i) Overpotential/overvoltage: although E° favours O2, the overpotential for O2 evolution is very high at the electrode. Cl2 has lower overpotential, so Cl2 is preferentially discharged.

(b)(ii) Acetic acid is a weak electrolyte; on dilution, degree of dissociation increases but the number of ions per unit volume (concentration) decreases. Since conductivity = κ depends on ion concentration, conductivity decreases.

questions.solution: For part (a): The cell Sn(s) | Sn²⁺ || H⁺ | H₂(g) | Pt(s) has Sn as the anode (oxidation) and H⁺/H₂ as the cathode (reduction). Cell reaction: Sn(s) + 2H⁺(aq) → Sn²⁺(aq) + H₂(g). E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.00 − (−0.14) = +0.14 V. Number of electrons transferred n = 2. Using Nernst equation: E = E° − (0.0591/2) × log Q, where Q = [Sn²⁺] / [H⁺]² = 0.004 / (0.02)² = 0.004 / 0.0004 = 10. E = 0.14 − (0.02955) × log(10) = 0.14 − 0.02955 × 1 = 0.14 − 0.0296 ≈ 0.11 V. For part (b)(i): Although the standard electrode potential of O₂/H₂O (+1.23 V) is lower than that of Cl₂/Cl⁻ (+1.36 V), suggesting O₂ should be preferentially discharged, in practice Cl₂ is liberated. This is because the overpotential (extra voltage needed beyond the thermodynamic value) for O₂ liberation at a platinum/graphite electrode is very high, while the overpotential for Cl₂ liberation is relatively low. This kinetic factor (overpotential) overrides the thermodynamic prediction, and Cl₂ is preferentially discharged. For part (b)(ii): Acetic acid (CH₃COOH) is a weak electrolyte. Its conductivity (κ) depends on both the degree of dissociation and the concentration of ions. On dilution, the degree of dissociation increases, but the total number of ions per unit volume of solution decreases because the solution becomes more dilute. Since conductivity is proportional to the number of ions per unit volume, the net effect is a decrease in conductivity on dilution.

questions.text_english:
(B)(a) Write the anode and cathode reactions and the overall cell reaction occurring in a lead storage battery during its use.
(b) Calculate the potential for half-cell containing 0.01 M K₂Cr₂O₇(aq), 0.01 M Cr³⁺(aq) and 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ M H⁺(aq).
The half cell reaction is: Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) + 14H⁺(aq) + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺(aq) + 7H₂O(l)
and the standard electrode potential is given as E° = 1.33 V.
[Given : log 10 = 1]

key_points: (a) Anode: Pb(s) + SO4^2-(aq) → PbSO4(s) + 2e-; Cathode: PbO2(s) + 4H+(aq) + SO4^2-(aq) + 2e- → PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l); Overall: Pb + PbO2 + 2H2SO4 → 2PbSO4 + 2H2O.

questions.solution: For part (a) – Lead storage battery reactions during discharge: At the anode (oxidation): Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2e⁻. At the cathode (reduction): PbO₂(s) + 4H⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) + 2e⁻ → PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l). Overall cell reaction: Pb(s) + PbO₂(s) + 2H₂SO₄(aq) → 2PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l). For part (b): The concentrations are [Cr₂O₇²⁻] = 0.01/2 = 0.005 M (since K₂Cr₂O₇ → 2K⁺ + Cr₂O₇²⁻, so [Cr₂O₇²⁻] = 0.01 M; however using as given = 0.01 M), [Cr³⁺] = 0.01 M, [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ M, n = 6. Reaction quotient Q = [Cr³⁺]² / ([Cr₂O₇²⁻][H⁺]¹⁴) = (0.01)² / (0.01 × (10⁻⁴)¹⁴) = 10⁻⁴ / (0.01 × 10⁻⁵⁶) = 10⁻⁴ / 10⁻⁵⁸ = 10⁵⁴. Using Nernst: E = E° − (0.0591/n) × log Q = 1.33 − (0.0591/6) × 54 = 1.33 − (0.00985 × 54) = 1.33 − 0.532 = 0.798 V ≈ 0.80 V.
